v19-4.candidate: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rhapsakes, whom his master the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with words which the Lord your God has heard. Take up a prayer for the remnant that remains.’
v19-4.close: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all Rhapsakes’s words, whom his master the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with words which the Lord your God has heard. Take up a prayer for the remnant that remains.’

v19-20.candidate: Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, Israel’s God: What you prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.
v19-20.close: Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, Israel’s God: What you did pray to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.

v19-23.candidate: Through your messengers you reproached the Lord and said, “With the multitude of my chariots I shall climb the mountain heights, Lebanon’s flanks. I cut down its cedar’s height, its choice cypresses, and came to the melon of its farthest part, the woodland of its Carmel.
v19-23.close: Through your messengers you did reproach the Lord and did say, “With the multitude of my chariots I shall climb the mountain heights, Lebanon’s flanks. I cut down its cedar’s height, its choice cypresses, and came to the melon of its farthest part, the woodland of its Carmel.
v19-23.display:
Through your messengers you reproached the Lord and said,
“With the multitude of my chariots I shall climb the mountain heights, Lebanon’s flanks.
I cut down its cedar’s height, its choice cypresses,
and came to the melon of its farthest part, the woodland of its Carmel.

v19-35.candidate: By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, all were dead bodies.
v19-35.close: By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.

v19-22.display:
Whom have you reproached and blasphemed?
Against whom have you raised your voice?
You have lifted your eyes on high against Israel’s Holy One!

v19-24.display:
I cooled and drank foreign waters,
and with my foot’s tread I dried up all rivers of enclosure.”

v19-25.display:
I formed it; now I brought it.
It became a carrying away into exiles of fighting men—fortified cities.

v19-26.display:
Their inhabitants grew weak in hand, cowered, and were ashamed.
They became field grass or green herbage,
rooftop grass, and a trampling before one standing.

v19-27.display:
I know your sitting, your going out, your coming in,
and your anger against Me.

v19-28.display:
Because you were angry with Me and your arrogance rose to My ears,
I shall put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips,
and turn you back by the road on which you came.

v19-29.display:
This shall be the sign for you:
You shall eat this year what grows by itself, and in the second year what sprouts.
In the third, sowing, harvest, and planting vineyards;
you shall eat their fruit.

v19-30.display:
The rescued remnant of Judah’s house shall again take root downward
and bear fruit upward.

v19-31.display:
For a remnant shall come out from Jerusalem,
and one escaping from Mount Zion.
The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.
